name: Saoud Rizwan
bio: Founder and CEO of Cline, an open-source AI coding agent for software development workflows.

talks.title: Open Source Is Dead. Long Live Open Source.

positions.claim: The community and contribution side of open source is no longer worth cultivating, because software is cheap to build and third-party contributions carry supply-chain risk.
Anthropic and OpenAI moved from API businesses into the application layer specifically to build a moat for when models commoditize.
The subsidize-then-lock-in strategy will not work; buyers will switch to whichever option gives the best value per dollar regardless of feature parity.
Open-weights models have reached the point where raw intelligence lead is no longer the decisive factor for most work.
Intelligence is better placed in the system and guardrails around the model than in the model itself, reducing reliance on both the model and the developer's judgment.
GLM outperformed Opus on a real Cline repo bug in cost and code quality, using 2x tokens at half the cost while Opus broke the production build.
Inference on a 1-trillion-parameter LLM will cost roughly 90% less by 2030, driven by ~$3T of capex and 100+ GW of new data center capacity.
Industries standardize on whatever they can build on top of, even when it is not the best available option.
American labs should release more open-weights models while keeping their research closed, since open weights enable copycats but not leapfrogging.
If foreign open-weights models become the industry standard, safety investment by Anthropic and OpenAI loses influence over how the technology develops.
Open source status was necessary for Cline's success, because it let developers inspect the code and trust it while spending heavily on API calls.
Enterprises will increasingly build their own internal routing and tooling around cheaper models, accepting the loss of the newest features from tools like Claude Code.
